title: Asymmetric Cavity Positioning for Dual Stopband Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Breaking the symmetry of the Fabry-Perot structure by using different mirror stack counts on each side of the cavity allows better optimization of the two asymmetric stopbands (1400-1500 nm vs 1600-1700 nm) while maintaining high 1550 nm transmittance.
design_principle: The two stopbands are at different wavelength offsets from 1550 nm (150 nm below vs 150 nm above). An asymmetric mirror design can tune the reflectance spectrum shape differently on each side of the passband, potentially achieving better suppression in both bands than a symmetric design with the same total layer count.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses in nm for all 11 layers
relative thickness ratio between input-side and substrate-side mirror stacks
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count is 11 (well under 30 limit)
asymmetric structure requires careful deposition sequence control
different mirror counts may affect stress balance
expected_advantages: Independent control of each stopband edge
May achieve better dual-band suppression than symmetric design
Same layer count budget as route_01 but different topology
known_risks: Asymmetry may reduce peak transmittance at 1550 nm
Optimization space is larger and may converge slower
May favor one stopband at expense of the other
execution_request_english: Design an asymmetric Fabry-Perot narrowband bandpass filter for 1550 nm LiDAR reception. Incident medium is air. Substrate is Fused Silica. Use only Ta2O5 (Gao) (high index) and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (low index) materials. Stack topology: Air | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao)(cavity) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Fused Silica. This is 11 layers total (4 pairs on input side, 6 pairs on substrate side, plus one cavity layer). Optimize all individual layer thicknesses in nanometers. Target wavelength is 1550 nm at normal incidence. Maximize transmittance at 1550 nm with soft target ≥0.95. Minimize transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Total layers must not exceed 30.
